To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the meanings of words are interactionally achieved through recurrent syntactic frames, that are underpinned and constrained by aspects abstracted lexical meanings.

(i) participants in everyday interactions draw from recurrent syntactic frames and interactional processes to co-construct the meanings of words in locally situated ways, and (ii) the locally situated meanings that participants co-construct are underpinned and afforded by aspects of abstract lexical meanings, but are nevertheless shaped for locally-situation purposes.

the meanings of bogs, lawyers and teachers are locally accomplished in interaction through the recurrent practices for doing so, and that those meanings are underpinned, but not determined, by aspects of the abstracted meanings of those words.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which speakers of a language use the resources of the language, and the ways in which the language itself shapes those uses.
the interactional achievement, and the social action(s) for which words are used.
how speakers use language to achieve word meanings in everyday encounters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the meaning of a word is interactionally achieved in-situ in a given sequence, and that this meaning may draw from, but also may depart from, the abstracted meanings of words as they are used in other contexts, and as they are recorded in dictionaries.
the meanings of words are not only contextually and interactionally contingent, but that they are also systematically constrained and afforded by recurrent sequential practices.
the meaning of a word is interactionally constructed, and is not a fixed entity, but is a dynamic process, and the meaning is a function of the social and cultural context in which it is used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the meaning of words are achieved through interactional means, and that these are systematically constrained by recurrent syntactic frames and abstracted word meanings.
words are used in interaction, and that their meanings are interactionally accomplished.
words do not have meaning, but that words are used to do meaning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the meanings of words are achieved through the recurrent practices that participants draw on for doing so.
, rather than being fixed, word meanings are interactionally achieved and that the meanings of words in context can be seen as emergent, dynamic and situated.
word meanings may be understood as a dynamic interplay of abstracted and situated aspects.
